The equiatomic VCoNi MEA were prepared from pure elements with purities higher than 99.9% via arc melting under a Ti gettered high purity argon atmosphere. The master ingots were flipped and completely re-melted at least 4 times to ensure chemical composition homogeneity
and then drop casted into a Cu mold with a size of 100 mm × 20 mm × 10 mm

parameters.atmosphere: evacuated and Ar backfilled quartz tube

evidence.quote: The rectangular samples were sealed in an evacuated and Ar backfilled quartz tubes, and then were homogenized at 1473 K for 24 h followed by water quenching.

parameters.deformation: 82% total reduction (0.3-0.5 mm per pass, 20 passes, to 1.8 mm)

evidence.quote: Cold rolling was conducted on the homogenized samples with an approximately 0.3 – 0.5 mm per pass. The thickness of samples was finally reduced to 1.8 mm after 20 passes with a total reduction of 82%.
After rolling, the rolled samples were annealed at 1373 K for 30 min and immediately water quenched to obtain fully recrystallized structures.
All the diffraction peaks can be indexed as a single FCC phase structure.
VCoNi alloy with FCC single phase exhibited excellent combination of strength and ductility
The homogeneous equiaxed grain structures are observed in the specimen, and many of the grains are found to contain annealing twins
many of the grains are found to contain annealing twins, which is in accordance with earlier reports
It can be seen that the dislocation cells and the intersected coplanar slip bands developed after deformation ( Fig. 5 a).
The average spacing between slip bands is about 30 nm, less than that in the deformed VCoNi specimens at 293 K
the profuse lamellar structures with an average width of 13 nm ( Fig. 5 c) are also observed, which are verified as {111} twins from the SAED patterns
However, an obvious σ phase is observed in the specimen after the tensile test at 473 K and 573 K, indicating that a dynamic precipitation occurred during deformation
the σ phases with an average size of 0.1 μ m distribute discretely in grain interiors and at grain boundaries of the deformed specimen at 573 K.
